title-group.article-title: Eribulin versus taxane as first-line chemotherapy combined with dual HER2 blockade in patients with HER2-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer: final survival outcomes of the JBCRG-M06/EMERALD study☆

sec.title: Background
sec.p: The phase III JBCRG-M06/EMERALD study was the first to show noninferior progression-free survival (PFS) of eribulin to taxane, combined with dual human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) blockade (trastuzumab plus pertuzumab), as a first-line treatment for HER2-positive locally advanced breast cancer or metastatic breast cancer (LABC/MBC). We report final survival outcomes and biomarker analyses of the EMERALD trial.

sec.title: Patients and methods
sec.p: Patients with HER2-positive LABC/MBC were randomly assigned 1:1 to either eribulin or physician-choice taxane (docetaxel or paclitaxel), both combined with trastuzumab plus pertuzumab, as first-line chemotherapy. PFS and overall survival (OS) were assessed through 30 June 2023 for PFS and 31 December 2024 for OS. Survival outcomes were compared between the eribulin and taxane groups and according to circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) detection of PIK3CA mutations (PIK3CAm+; E542K, E545K, H1047R, and N345K single nucleotide variants) or HER2 amplification (HER2 amp+; ERBB2 copy number >2.5).

sec.title: Results
sec.p: Median OS was 78.5 months [95% confidence interval (CI) 64.3-not reached (NR)] for eribulin and was NR for taxane, with a hazard ratio of 1.25 (95% CI 0.92-1.71, log-rank P = 0.19). The 60-month OS rates were 59.7% and 65.2% for eribulin and taxane, respectively. Median OS and 60-month OS rates were numerically lower in ctDNA PIK3CAm+ patients, and greater in ctDNA HER2 amp+ patients for all patients and with stratification by treatment group. There were no statistical interactions between treatment group with either ctDNA PIK3CAm or ctDNA HER2 amp status. Similar patterns were observed for PFS.

sec.title: Conclusion
sec.p: Final survival analysis revealed that median OS exceeded 6 years with eribulin or physician-choice taxane, combined with trastuzumab plus pertuzumab, as first-line chemotherapy for HER2-positive LABC/MBC, with no significant differences between the two groups. ctDNA PIK3CAm+ status was a poor prognostic factor. ctDNA HER2 amp+ was associated with longer survival.
Key words: dual HER2 blockade, eribulin mesylate, HER2 amplification, locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer, PIK3CA mutation

list-item.p: We report final survival outcomes and prognostic biomarkers of the EMERALD trial in patients with HER2-positive LABC/MBC.
Patients received eribulin or taxane, both combined with trastuzumab and pertuzumab.
Median OS was 78.5 months in the eribulin group and was NR in the taxane group (HR 1.25, P = 0.19).
OS and PFS tended to be worse in ctDNA PIK3CAm+ versus PIK3CAm− patients and better in ctDNA HER2 amp+ versus HER2 amp− patients.
Eribulin is an effective alternative to taxanes as a partner to dual HER2 blockade in patients with HER2-positive LABC/MBC.

sec.p: Collection date 2026 Aug.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive breast cancer is an aggressive subtype that accounts for up to 20% of all breast cancers and is associated with a high rate of disease progression despite HER2-targeted therapies.1 There remains a need for further treatments for recurrent or metastatic breast cancer (MBC), especially in a first-line setting.2,3 Following the CLEOPATRA trial,4, 5, 6 dual HER2 blockade with trastuzumab (H) plus pertuzumab (P) plus a taxane became the standard first-line therapy for HER2-positive MBC7, 8, 9; however, taxane-associated toxicities limit its tolerability.10

Eribulin mesylate, a nontaxane microtubule dynamics inhibitor, has gained attention as a potential alternative to taxanes used in combination with dual HER2 blockade for treating MBC. It has shown overall survival (OS) benefit in pivotal phase III trials,11, 12, 13 meta-analysis,14 and real-world studies,15, 16, 17 with a greater effect on OS than on progression-free survival (PFS).

We conducted the randomized open-label phase III EMERALD study, which was the first to show noninferiority of eribulin to taxane (docetaxel or paclitaxel) when used with dual HER2 blockade (H plus P), as first-line chemotherapy for HER2-positive locally advanced breast cancer (LABC) or MBC.18 In the primary analysis, the median PFS was 14.0 and 12.9 months in the eribulin and taxane groups, respectively [hazard ratio (HR) 0.95], confirming the noninferiority of the study regimen. The incidence of adverse events was similar between the two groups, despite the longer treatment duration with eribulin than with taxanes (median duration of treatment: 28.1 weeks with eribulin versus 18.1 and 20.5 weeks with docetaxel and paclitaxel, respectively). Eribulin was also associated with a longer maintenance of quality of life.18

At the time of the earlier report, the OS data were still immature because median OS was not reached (NR) in the eribulin group, compared with 65.3 months in the taxane group. Here, we report the final analysis of OS after ≥5 years of follow-up. In addition, we sought to identify biomarkers that may be predictive of treatment responses.

Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), a subset of cell-free DNA released into the bloodstream by tumor cells through apoptosis, offers early insight into mechanisms of cancer treatment resistance. In clinical practice, ctDNA serves not only as a prognostic marker but also as a tool to tailor therapy, providing real-time information on treatment response, tumor biology, and disease evolution.19, 20, 21 Its ability to dynamically and noninvasively track genomic alterations such as HER2 status and PIK3CA mutations makes it particularly valuable, considering the prognostic relevance of alterations in these genes.22, 23, 24, 25 By integrating ctDNA analysis into clinical workflows, clinicians can personalize and adapt cancer treatments in real time, especially in patients with HER2-positive or PIK3CA-mutated BC.26 PIK3CA mutations are among the most common genetic alterations in BC, present in over one-third of cases. These mutations are particularly enriched in luminal and HER2-positive subtypes, and have a significant impact on prognosis.25,27 Biomarker analysis from the CLEOPATRA study demonstrated that HER2 is the only suitable marker gene for selecting H plus P-based therapy for patients with HER2-positive MBC. Additionally, the genes HER2, HER3, and PIK3CA were identified as relevant prognostic factors.28 As part of the EMERALD study, we carried out ctDNA biomarker analysis using droplet digital PCR to assess PIK3CA mutations and HER2 amplification.

sec.title: Study design and patients
sec.p: The JBCRG-M06/EMERALD was a multicenter, randomized, open-label, parallel-group phase III trial that investigated the noninferiority of eribulin plus H plus P against a taxane (docetaxel or paclitaxel) plus H plus P as first-line treatment for HER2-positive LABC or MBC (Supplementary Figure S1, available at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esmoop.2026.108325). Full details of the methods have been published previously.18,29 Key eligibility criteria were a histological diagnosis of HER2-positive LABC/MBC, age 20-70 years, and no prior cytotoxic chemotherapy for LABC/MBC [other than trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1)].29 Patients could have received hormonal or anti-HER2 therapy alone, or in combination, to treat recurrent disease.

Eligible patients were randomly assigned (ratio 1 : 1) to the eribulin or taxane groups to receive eribulin (1.4 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8) or a taxane (docetaxel 75 mg/m2 on day 1 or paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15), in a 21-day cycle, each with H plus P (Supplementary Figure S1, available at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esmoop.2026.108325). Randomization was stratified by history of perioperative use of taxane, prior treatment with T-DM1 for recurrent disease, and presence of visceral metastases. Treatments were continued until disease progression, unmanageable toxicity, or consent withdrawal. The recommended minimum treatment duration was six cycles.

sec.title: Ethical considerations
sec.p: The study adhered to the Declaration of Helsinki and relevant ethical guidelines and was approved by the Certified Review Board of Fukushima Medical University (approval no. F2018005) as well as the ethics committee of each participating institution at study initiation, with additional approval obtained for this follow-up study. All patients provided informed consent at the start of the study. Additional consent was considered unnecessary for this follow-up because all data were collected from the patients’ medical records without additional patient participation. The study was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03264547) and the University Hospital Medical Information Network (UMIN000027938).

sec.title: Outcomes
sec.p: The primary endpoint of the JBCRG-M06/EMERALD study was PFS, which was determined by the investigators according to the revised RECIST version 1.1. It was calculated as the time from enrollment to disease progression or death from any cause. Patients without disease progression were censored at the time of the last determination of PFS. OS, a prespecified secondary endpoint, was defined as the time from random assignment to death from any cause. Data were censored if patients were alive or lost to follow-up. Patients who started endocrine therapy without disease progression were censored because the addition of endocrine therapy to maintenance anti-HER2 therapy was not permitted, and endocrine therapy after confirmed disease progression was considered as a post-progression treatment. This 5-year follow-up analysis presents updated PFS and OS (cut-off dates: 30 June 2023 for PFS and 31 December 2024 for OS).

For ctDNA analysis, blood was collected at baseline and/or on day 1 of cycle 2. Droplet digital PCR was used to detect single nucleotide variants (SNVs) in PIK3CA E542K, E545K, H1047R, and N345K, and copy number variants in ERBB2. The presence of any of these SNVs was defined as ctDNA PIK3CA mutations (PIK3CAm). ctDNA HER2 amplification (HER2 amp) was defined as an ERBB2 copy number of >2.5.

sec.title: Statistical analyses
sec.p: OS, a prespecified secondary endpoint, was compared between the eribulin and taxane groups using the Kaplan–Meier method with the log-rank test for intergroup comparison, in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population comprising all randomly assigned patients. Additionally, survival curves were plotted using the Kaplan–Meier method for patients with (+) or without (−) ctDNA PIK3CAm or HER2 amp, which were prespecified biomarkers, among those whose status was determined at any point during the treatment period. A forest plot was generated to compare OS across patient subgroups and to determine HRs with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The level of statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. The study was powered to detect differences in the primary endpoint (i.e. PFS), with the sample size calculation described previously.18,29 Statistical analyses were carried out using SAS version. 9.4 (SAS Institute Inc., Cary, NC).

sec.title: Patients
sec.p: As previously reported,18 the ITT population comprised 446 patients, with 224 in the eribulin group and 222 in the taxane group. The median follow-up time was 48.6 months (interquartile range 36.9-65.4 months). Table 1 shows the baseline characteristics and ctDNA status of the enrolled patients. Baseline characteristics were generally balanced between the treatment groups. The median age of the 446 enrolled patients in the ITT was 56.0 (range 29-70) years. Overall, 25.3% of patients were premenopausal and 72.2% were postmenopausal. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status was 0 in 83.2% and 1 in 16.1%. Disease-free interval was <24 months in 9.0%, ≥24 months in 31.8%, and 59.0% were diagnosed as de novo stage IV. The ctDNA analysis population comprised 159 and 154 patients in the eribulin and taxane groups, respectively. ctDNA HER2 amp+ was less frequent in the eribulin group [85 (53.5%)] than in the taxane group [102 (66.2%)].

sec.title: OS according to treatment
sec.p: Figure 1A shows the OS results in the ITT population. The median OS was 78.5 months (95% CI 64.3-NR) in the eribulin group and NR in the taxane group (HR 1.25, 95% CI 0.92-1.71; log-rank P = 0.19). OS events occurred in 90/224 and 72/222 in the eribulin and taxane groups, respectively. The 60-month OS rates were 59.7% (95% CI 52.3-66.2) and 65.2% (95% CI 57.8-71.7), respectively. There were no significant differences in OS between the eribulin and taxane groups in any subgroup (Figure 1B).

sec.title: OS according to ctDNA PIK3CAm status and treatment
sec.p: ctDNA was analyzed in 313 patients (159 and 154 patients in the eribulin and taxane groups, respectively). The OS results based on PIK3CAm status in all patients and according to treatment group are shown in Figure 2A and B, respectively. In the overall ctDNA population, OS was numerically shorter [median OS: 43.2 (95% CI 27.8-61.7) months versus NR] and the 60-month OS rate was lower [38.5% (95% CI 26.2-50.6) versus 67.4% (60.6-73.3)] in PIK3CAm+ patients than in PIK3CAm− patients (Figure 2A). A similar pattern was observed when patients were stratified by treatment group (Figure 2B). No interaction between treatment group and PIK3CAm status was apparent.

sec.title: OS according to ctDNA HER2 amp status and treatment
sec.p: The OS results based on HER2 amp status in all patients and according to treatment group are shown in Figure 3A and B, respectively. OS tended to be longer in HER2 amp+ patients than in HER2 amp− patients, with median OS of NR (95% CI 69.7-NR) versus 65.3 (95% CI 51.3-NR) months, respectively. The 60-month OS rate also tended to be greater in HER amp+ patients [64.7% (95% CI 56.8-71.6)] than in HER amp− patients [54.9% (95% CI 45.1-63.7)] (Figure 3A). This pattern was also observed when patients were stratified by treatment group (Figure 3B). No interaction between treatment group and HER2 amp was apparent.

sec.title: PFS according to ctDNA PIK3CAm and ctDNA HER2 amp status and treatment
sec.p: The PFS results for PIK3CAm status and HER2 amp, by treatment group, are shown in Figure 4A and B, respectively. Similar to the results for OS, PFS tended to be longer in PIK3CAm− and HER2 amp+ patients in both treatment groups. By HER2 amp status, among HER2 amp+ patients, PFS tended to be longer in the eribulin subgroup than in the taxane subgroup, whereas no clear differences were observed between the two treatments among HER2 amp− patients.

sec.title: Post-progression treatments
sec.p: Supplementary Table S1, available at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esmoop.2026.108325, presents data on treatments administered immediately after disease progression during the study treatment. In the taxane group, T-DM1 and trastuzumab deruxtecan tended to be used more frequently. In the eribulin group, the combination of eribulin plus H plus P was more commonly used. The patterns of use of other post-progression treatments were generally similar between the two groups.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: The EMERALD study was the first study to demonstrate noninferior PFS of eribulin versus a taxane (docetaxel or paclitaxel) as part of first-line treatment combined with H plus P for HER2-positive LABC or MBC.18 Here, we reported the results of a longer follow-up. No significant difference was seen in OS between the eribulin and taxane groups, with median OS exceeding 6 years in both groups, although the OS rate tended to be slightly lower in the eribulin group. We also investigated possible prognostic factors and identified that blood ctDNA PIK3CAm positivity was a poor prognostic factor because OS and PFS tended to be shorter in PIK3CAm+ patients than in PIK3CAm− patients, and this deleterious impact of PIK3CAm+ status was evident in both treatment groups. By comparison, ctDNA HER2 amp+ patients tended to show more favorable prognosis in terms of OS and PFS than HER2 amp− patients, with a similar prognostic impact in both treatment groups. Considering these findings, we suspect that the lower proportion of HER2 amp+ patients in the eribulin group might contribute to its slightly lower OS compared with the taxane group.

The increasing use of precision/targeted therapies is placing greater reliance on ctDNA analyses to detect genetic factors and identify potential therapeutic targets or actionable mutations.19, 20, 21 In this cohort of patients with LABC or MBC treated with dual HER2 blockade and either eribulin or a taxane, we found that ctDNA PIK3CAm positivity was associated with poor prognosis whereas ctDNA HER2 amp was associated with more favorable prognosis across both groups. These findings are consistent with those reported in a biomarker analysis of the CLEOPATRA study,28 in which significant prognostic variables included HER2 protein (P = 0.05), HER2 mRNA (P = 0.008), HER3 mRNA (P = 0.03), and PIK3CAm positivity (P < 0.001). Like us, the authors noted that PIK3CAm+ status was associated with worse prognosis, and high HER2 protein/mRNA expression (akin to HER2 amp+ in our study) was associated with better prognosis.

Prior studies have identified PIK3CAm positivity as a prognostic factor in breast cancer. Mutations in this gene were reported in approximately one-third (35.5%) of patients with breast cancer in a Japanese nationwide dataset.30 The protein phosphatidylinositol-3 phosphate kinase (PI3K), encoded by PIK3CA, is a key effector of HER2 signaling.31 Mutations in PIK3CA may lead to constitutive activation of PI3K, which may exert an inhibitory effect on HER2 signaling.32 Continuous PI3K signaling may therefore provide an escape mechanism, even in the presence of HER blockade.33 Accordingly, HER2-positive PIK3CAm+ MBC appears to be a subtype of MBC with worse prognosis.28,34,35 Such cases may benefit from dual HER2 blockade combined with another therapy, such as eribulin or a taxane, together with a PI3K inhibitor or another drug targeting the PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway.36 Since the proportion of patients with ctDNA PIK3CAm+ status was similar in the eribulin and taxane groups (22.6% and 24.7%, respectively), we surmise that other factors might contribute to the slight difference in OS.

The longer PFS observed in the eribulin subgroup compared with the taxane subgroup, particularly among HER2 amp+ patients, was not reflected in the OS outcomes, which instead showed better results in the taxane subgroup. This suggests that ctDNA HER2 amp+ is a positive prognostic factor but may not necessarily predict OS. The former is consistent with abundant evidence showing that HER2 amp+ patients are generally more responsive to HER2-targeting therapies owing to increased HER2 protein expression.37, 38, 39 However, the effectiveness of HER2 blockade is attenuated in some patients, and a link between HER2 status and PIK3CA mutations was reported in one study showing higher rates of PIK3CA mutations in HER2-low patients.40 Such patients might therefore be less likely to show a response to dual HER2 blockade and require treatment with alternative therapies. As shown in Figure 3A, the HER2 amp+ patients had a better prognosis than the HER2 amp− patients. However, the proportion of HER2 amp+ patients was higher in the taxane subgroup (102/154; 66.2%) than in the eribulin subgroup (85/159; 53.5%) (Figure 1B), which may have contributed to the better OS observed in taxane subgroup.

We should also acknowledge the possibility that post-progression treatments contributed to the different patterns of PFS and OS among these subgroups of patients. T-DM1 and trastuzumab deruxtecan were used slightly more frequently in the taxane group, and eribulin combined with H plus P was used more frequently in the eribulin group. Otherwise, the post-progression treatments were generally similar between the two groups. The more frequent use of eribulin plus H plus P in the eribulin group may reflect cases in which treatment was continued despite radiographic disease progression because disease control was clinically maintained and the progression was not considered clinically significant. Alternatively, in the present study, H plus P plus chemotherapy was intended to be continued for at least six cycles. If adverse events occurred thereafter, chemotherapy could be discontinued and H plus P could be continued. Progression during maintenance H plus P was counted as a disease progression event. Therefore, some patients who initially responded to eribulin plus H plus P subsequently discontinued eribulin, and later progressed on H plus P alone may have been retreated with eribulin after disease progression. This also applied to taxane plus H plus P; however, taxanes may have been less frequently reintroduced after disease progression because of concerns regarding toxicity.

Based on recent findings from the phase III DESTINY-Breast09 trial,41 which demonstrated that trastuzumab deruxtecan plus P significantly improved PFS compared with the standard regimen of taxane plus H plus P, this combination may represent a first-line treatment option for HER2-positive advanced or metastatic BC, although an OS benefit has not yet been established. An alternative strategy may be to initiate treatment with H plus P plus chemotherapy, followed by maintenance therapy with endocrine therapy plus palbociclib for hormone receptor–positive patients and H plus P plus tucatinib for hormone receptor–negative patients. Thus, although differences in treatment lines preclude direct extrapolation of the data, the findings from the present study may provide useful insights when selecting subsequent treatment options, particularly regarding which chemotherapy agent (taxane or eribulin) to combine with dual HER2 blockade.

sec.title: Limitations
sec.p: The main limitations to the EMERALD study are described in more detail in the earlier report.18 In the context of the current analyses, some additional limitations should be mentioned. In particular, not all patients underwent ctDNA testing, which may introduce some selection bias. Additionally, the study was not specifically powered to detect a statistically significant difference in OS between the eribulin and taxane groups. Likewise, the study was not powered to compare OS/PFS among the subgroups of patients divided by ctDNA PIK3CAm and ctDNA HER2 amp status. Therefore, our findings may require validation in a larger cohort. Nevertheless, the prognostic effects of ctDNA PIK3CAm+ and ctDNA HER2 amp+ are consistent with those of other studies, supporting the generalizability of these results. Finally, we should consider the possibility that slight differences in post-progression treatments might influence OS.

sec.title: Conclusion
sec.p: The present study demonstrated valuable effects of first-line eribulin plus H plus P on OS in patients with HER2-positive LABC/MBC. The median OS exceeded 6 years in the eribulin and taxane groups, but the OS rate was numerically better in the taxane group, which might be influenced by imbalances in ctDNA HER2 amplification status or other factors. Consistent with prior studies, blood ctDNA PIK3CAm status was a poor prognostic factor; however, no interaction with treatment regimen was observed. ctDNA HER2 amp+ patients tended to have longer survival (PFS and OS) than ctDNA HER2 amp− patients. The slightly lower trend in OS observed in the eribulin group might be due to a lower proportion of ctDNA HER2 amp+ patients in that group than in the taxane group. Overall, these results support earlier analysis of the EMERALD study, showing that eribulin is noninferior to taxane in terms of PFS, which translates into a clinically meaningful OS, in patients with HER2-positive LABC/MBC receiving dual HER2 blockade.
